- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike (≥5% from prior), true outcome often corrects downward within next 5–7 days; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above prior high.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80) after a spike, model often fails to adjust; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% in subsequent periods.  
- If sentiment is neutral or negative (≤0.1) and model is rising, forecast may be overconfident; apply downward bias of 2–5% if recent 3-day average is rising.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days); adjust downward by 1–3% for first 5 days if sentiment is flat or negative.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent spike (e.g., 0.5–0.8) followed by 0.00, model often overcorrects; reduce forecast by 2–4% in next 3–5 days.
